# PR #3745: Patch: the AI's search keeps room for a plan whose payoff lands next turn

Closes #3696

Both halves of the plan are built, each with its own ruling, tests and docs. Gate and perf pass and match base. One thing needs a person's attention: in a small local sweep, the branch casts Mind Games **less** often than base, and the branch's report would shadow-ban it.

## What changed

- **R3696000, the shortlist** (`crates/ai/src/decide.rs`).
  - A new check, `leaves_own_delayed`, asks whether a line ends the turn (`Passed` or `Yielded`, the lines the reply answers) with a delayed effect of the AI's own that it did not hold before, such as a countdown or a next-turn reward.
  - When none of the six lines `shortlist_lines` picks has one, it adds the best line that does, last, past the count and the per-action cap.
  - That is at most one more reply per decision. Because it comes last, a counter that runs short drops it first.
- **R3696001, the reply** (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`).
  - While the imagined opponent holds a card the AI saw arrive that its own cleanup will discard (Temporary with 1 left, `doomed_known_card`), `known_play` judges every play, and standing still, after the opponent ends its turn (`judged`, through a new `at_close` flag on `best_try`).
  - A card that guesses an unrevealed secret of the AI's (Fortify Mind) is tried with one guess (`one_guess_per_card`). The guess is drawn before anything is weighed, on its own stream (`AI_GUESS_SEED`, the world's seed and the card's id), so it never depends on the secret.
  - Visible activations and defence switches behave as before.
- **Docs:** §9.9's reply bullet, `crates/ai/README.md` and `docs/polish/3-ai.md` gain both facts; both §11 paragraphs are in `spec/pending/3696.md`. There is no catalog change, so no patch fragment.

Each test fails with its half switched off. I checked by disabling each half for a moment:
- With the shortlist fix off, the decision test and shortlist tests 1 and 4 fail.
- With the turn-end comparison off, reply tests 1 and 2 fail.
- With the single guess off, reply tests 2 and 3 fail.

The eight tests:
- **`decide.rs`, four `r3696000_*` tests:**
  - the best delayed-payoff line keeps a place after six lines that outscore it;
  - no place is held back when there is no such line, or when one already made the cut;
  - none of these counts as a payoff: an effect the AI already held, one the other seat owns, or one on a line that is never replied to.
- **`tests/ai/meditative_plus.rs`, `r3696000_the_ai_still_casts_supply_drop_in_combat_mode_with_two_castable_units_in_hand`:** before the fix the AI played a Vanilla instead (`Play { instance_id: "c2", … lane: 1 }`).
- **`reply.rs`, three `r3696001_*` tests:**
  - the opponent plays the Fortify Mind it used to keep;
  - its guess is the same whichever choice the AI kept, and cancels the reward against exactly one of the three;
  - a revealed secret keeps every guess, and other world seeds draw other guesses.

- `cargo test -p jackioh-ai --lib --test ai`: 35 and 814 passed.

- `cargo jackioh spec check`: `1907 rulings, 4941 proofs, 62312 citations in 4113 files, 25346 links: ok`. `catalog check` and `patches check` also pass.

|---|---|---|
| `gate` ai-vs-random (17 needed) | 19/20 | 19/20 |
| `gate` ai-vs-greedy (10 needed) | 16/20 | 16/20 |
| `gate` hard-vs-easy (16 needed) | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| `gate perf`, slowest of 29 decisions | 40.3 ms, 408 nodes | 41.0 ms, 408 nodes |

```

base   | meditativeplus-004 | Jlockeed's Supply Drop | hard | cleared | 15/24 | 56 | 56 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -1.6 |
base   | meditative-022 | Mind Games | easy | cleared | 15/25 | 44 | 44 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -5.5 |
base   | meditative-022 | Mind Games | hard | cleared | 9/24 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -6.3 |
branch | meditativeplus-004 | Jlockeed's Supply Drop | easy | cleared | 13/24 | 26 | 26 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -2.0 |
branch | meditativeplus-004 | Jlockeed's Supply Drop | hard | cleared | 15/24 | 55 | 55 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -2.4 |
branch | meditative-022 | Mind Games | easy | neverPlayed | 15/25 | 48 | 48 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 | -3.6 |
branch | meditative-022 | Mind Games | hard | neverPlayed | 9/24 | 27 | 27 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | n/a |
```

Pass 1 was the same on both sides: Supply Drop clean; Mind Games `neverPlayed` at Easy (4/8 drawn, 17 turns on base, 18 on the branch) and at Hard (3/8, 11 turns).

The branch report ends "1 banned, 1 watched", and its `SHADOW_BAN` block lists `("meditative-022", "neverPlayed: hard: affordable in hand on 27 turns and playable on 27 over 24 pass-2 games, never played")`. | AI's hand, mana | base | shortlist fix only | reply fix only | branch (both) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mind Games, 2 | 20/20 | 20/20 | 20/20 | 20/20 |
| Mind Games + Vanilla, 3 | 20/20 | 20/20 | 3/20 | 3/20 |
| Mind Games + Vanilla, 2 | 20/20 | 20/20 | 4/20 | 4/20 |
| Mind Games + 2 Vanillas, 2 | 0/20 | 20/20 | 0/20 | 0/20 |

- Base already overrated Mind Games whenever a line with it reached the reply. It picked it over a 1-mana 4/4 on every seed, because its imagined opponent kept Fortify Mind and took all three penalties.
- The shortlist fix alone spreads that overrating to every board, as the issue predicted.
- With both fixes the opponent answers the card, and Mind Games is cast mostly when nothing cheaper competes.

So the branch casts Mind Games less, not more. The issue leaves that call to the gate, and the gate is unchanged. Supply Drop's rows barely move.

## Decisions the issue left open

- **Where the reply tests live:** in `reply.rs`'s own test module, not `tests/ai/reply.rs` or `secrets.rs`, because the functions they test are private.
- **The extra line:**
  - It is added last and outside the per-action cap. Putting it first was rejected: it would cost a better-ranked line its reply when the counter runs short. Holding it to the cap was rejected: it could never add a line whose first action already has two.
  - A larger node reserve was rejected because it shrinks every search.
  - Pricing delayed effects in the static score was rejected because the reply already weighs a countdown where it comes due (#1995).
- **The guess:**
  - One guess, drawn on its own stream. Weighing all three was rejected because it reads the secret through the evaluation (R185). Averaging them was rejected as three times the nodes.
  - Drawing from `options.rng` was rejected because it would move the decision's random stream.
  - A revealed secret is not a guess, so every play is tried, as before.
- **The turn-end comparison:** it applies only while a doomed known card is held. Doing it for every reply step was rejected as one more simulation per try.
- **Skipping the extra place on a short clock:** this needs no code of its own. The line is replied to last, and a clocked decision's replies stop at the hard stop (R3498000), so it is the first dropped.
- **One addition to the plan's ruling text:** R3696001 records a second accepted limit, below.

## Worth a second look

- **The AI's own Mind Games choice:** on each sampled world, the AI's choice meets that world's one drawn guess. In world 0 it can follow that guess; the finalists' average over the other worlds softens this. The guess itself never depends on the AI's choice.
- **Cost:** while a doomed known card is held, each `known_play` step costs 1 + n end-of-turn simulations (n ≤ `AI_REPLY.known_plays`). The gate's win counts and the pinned positions' reply counts (6, 5 and 6 lines) are the same on both sides.

# #3696: Patch: the AI's search keeps room for a plan whose payoff lands next turn
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some cards pay off a turn later: a supply drop that arrives next turn, or Mind Games, whose secret reward lands at the start of your next turn. The practice AI thinks through the opponent's answer for only a handful of its best-looking plans, and it picks that handful by a quick score that cannot see a payoff still to come. So "cast Mind Games and end the turn" looks like throwing two mana away, and it is cut before the AI ever weighs it. Once this is built, the AI always keeps one place in that handful for its best plan with a payoff still to come, and the opponent it imagines answers such cards as a person would.

## Why
- Only the top `finalists × lines_per_action` lines (3 × 2 = 6; `crates/ai/src/config.rs:66`, `:222`), ranked by the static score, reach the opponent's reply (`shortlist_lines`, `crates/ai/src/decide.rs:133-152`, called at `decide.rs:542`).
- The static evaluation (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`, `material`) prices almost none of the seat's own delayed effects. Countdowns are fired only inside the reply's score (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs:593-600`, #1995). A line whose value is a delayed reward therefore ranks on its cost alone, and one unit play tried in five lanes fills the six places first.
- The sweep of 2026-10-28 (`training/history/sweep-2026-10-28.md:220-243`): Jlockeed's Supply Drop was cast on 25 of 619 affordable turns at Hard and 53 of 417 at Easy, at a mean evaluation change of about −1.4 to −2.6; Mind Games on 12 of 470 at Hard and 46 of 351 at Easy, about −1.6 to −3.1. `the_ai_casts_supply_drop_in_combat_mode_against_three_3_health_units` (`crates/ai/tests/ai/meditative_plus.rs:342`) passes only because Supply Drop is the AI's only card there.
- Once Mind Games does reach the reply, the imagined opponent never plays its Fortify Mind. `best_try` (`reply.rs:284-319`) compares each play with the position now, where a winning guess changes nothing the evaluation reads (the reward it cancels is a delayed entry). So the opponent keeps the card, and cleanup discards it into all three penalties (`crates/cards/src/scripts/meditative/c022_1_fortify_mind.rs`, R862). Fixing the shortlist alone would make the AI overrate Mind Games.

## Proposal
1. `shortlist_lines` keeps one place for the best-scored line whose end holds a delayed entry of the seat's own that the root did not (a countdown or a next-turn reward), when the plain ranking left none in. That is at most one more reply a decision.
2. In the reply, an opponent holding a known Temporary card that cleanup will discard this turn compares its plays with the position after its turn ends, not before. A guess against the AI's secret is drawn from the world's own stream, so it never depends on the secret (R185, R860).

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/decide.rs`, `crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/meditative_plus.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/secrets.rs`, `crates/ai/tests/ai/reply.rs`
- SPEC §10.7; R185, R860, R861, R862, R864

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A `shortlist_lines` test: the best delayed-payoff line is kept when six other lines outscore it, and no place is held back when there is no such line or one already made the cut.
- [ ] A decision test: the Supply Drop board of `meditative_plus.rs:342`, with a castable unit added to the AI's hand, still casts Supply Drop in combat mode.
- [ ] A reply test: after the AI casts Mind Games, the imagined opponent plays Fortify Mind rather than letting it be discarded, and its guess is the same whichever choice the AI kept secret.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` passes and `cargo jackioh perf` stays within its budgets; the sweep rows for Supply Drop and Mind Games, before and after, are in the pull request.

## Size and risks
Small to medium: two functions and four tests. One more reply a decision costs time on a slow phone; the perf gate measures it, and the extra place can be skipped when the clock is short.
